title: Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-08-24
content:
Summary:
This week focused on reactive scaling after last weekend's spike in model training workloads and the follow-up capacity planning discussion for H4 Dedicated commitments. We also ran a brownout test in eu-west1 and validated autoscaling behaviour for cached KV-heavy workloads.

Highlights / Metrics (week of 2026-08-17 -> 2026-08-23):
- Fleet-wide GPU utilization (p95): 72% (up from 64% last week)
- Usable spare capacity (global): ~14% (target minimum = 12%)
- Region breakdown (spare GPUs, estimated nodes):
  - us-west1: 28 GPUs (~4 nodes) - spare shrinking due to Dedicated commitments
  - us-east1: 52 GPUs (~7 nodes) - healthy buffer
  - eu-west1: 16 GPUs (~3 nodes) - after brownout test regained 2 GPUs of spare capacity
  - ap-southeast1: 8 GPUs (~2 nodes) - low utilization, plan to re-locate some pods if demand picks up
- Average request latency change after prefix caching adjustment: 6% lower median token latency for chat workloads
- Cost note: spot eviction rate 1.6% (up 0.4ppt) during the spike; evaluating fallback warm pools

Incidents & Postmortem updates:
- INF-472: Intermittent 503s in eu-west1 during brownout test (2026-08-22 03:14 UTC).
  - Root cause: Under-provisioned warm pool for the canary service; autoscaler cooldown too long before adding dense nodes.
  - Mitigation implemented: reduced cooldown from 240s -> 90s and increased warm pool target by 1 node for eu-west1.
  - Follow-up: infra/sre to run chaos test next week and validate stable scaling under KV cache thrash (owner: Lena, due: 2026-08-31).

Capacity planning & Decisions:
- Dedicated capacity: Sales requested an additional 40 GPUs for Q4 trial customers. After sizing and simulation we recommend a phased add of 24 GPUs into us-west1 in early Sept, with burst capacity routing to us-east1 if needed. Action: create reserved pool conversion ticket (owner: Diego, JIRA INF-489).
- Autoscaling policy adjustments: For KV-heavy workloads we will lower target batch latency threshold from 120ms -> 90ms to favor adding nodes before latency spikes. Action: rollout config to canaries on 2026-08-26 (owner: Michael).
- Region placement policy: prefer heterogenous node types in us-east1 to handle both training and inference bursts. Ops to inventory current node SKUs and submit purchase schedule by 2026-09-07 (owner: Aisha).

Standup / Daily notes (select days):
- Mon 2026-08-17:
  - Quick sync: validated brownout plan, confirmed SRE on-call schedule, no high-priority customer alerts.
- Wed 2026-08-19:
  - Observed early signs of request skew to us-west1 from a large customer; throttling rules applied to prevent noisy-neighbor impact.
- Sat 2026-08-22:
  - Brownout test + incident INF-472; ran emergency scale and reverted non-essential batch jobs.

Meetings this week:
- Capacity planning (2026-08-20): Reviewed Q4 forecast, committed to not exceed 60% committed reserved addition without performance SLAs in place. Agreed to phased adds and automated routing for burst.
- SRE retro (2026-08-23): Focused on autoscaler cooldowns and warm pool sizing; prioritized adjustable cooldown per service.

Action items (owner - due):
- Diego - open reserved pool conversion ticket and attach simulation outputs (JIRA INF-489) - due 2026-08-27
- Michael - rollout autoscaler config changes to canary cluster - due 2026-08-26
- Aisha - node SKU inventory + procurement timeline - due 2026-09-07
- Lena - chaos test for KV cache thrash validation; include eviction and cold-start scenarios - due 2026-08-31
- SRE team - update runbook for brownout tests to include tighter guardrails around canary traffic routing - due 2026-08-28

Risks & asks:
- Risk: If spot eviction trend continues upward (>2.5%), unit economics for Hosted API could degrade; ask Procurement to prioritize staggered commitments for cheap persistent capacity.
- Ask for Product: freeze major model-onboarding in us-west1 between 2026-09-05 -> 2026-09-12 to allow capacity additions and rebalancing. Product owner: Priya (cc: infra).
- Ask for Sales: any new Dedicated deals that target us-west1 in Q4 please flag to infra at least 4 weeks prior so we can reserve capacity.

Notes / misc:
- Working draft of the H4 Capacity Plan uploaded to Confluence; link in linked_artifacts. Please review especially the assumptions sheet (traffic growth, model mix).
- Will run a cross-team sync next Wed (2026-08-26) to finalize autoscaler rollout window and canary list.

Attachments / artifacts referenced:
- Simulation outputs (attached to JIRA INF-489)
- Brownout test logs (s3://redwood-logs/infra/brownout/eu-west1/2026-08-22)
- Autoscaler config diff (GitHub PR above)

If anything is missing or you'd like a deeper dive on region-specific numbers, ping me or drop requests in #infra-capacity.

-- Michael
